I'm debugging a shared Project Maya 1.1.34 service using parallel native requests. A synthetic background Responses request was created with store:true and background:true. Closing its SSE reader did not stop the job. Its cancel call returned in_progress after about five seconds, then a later snapshot said cancelled. Meanwhile the native wrapper warned that the engine may still be writing it after the STOP drain timeout. Can I safely say the GPU is freed and submit dependent work now?

Reconnecting with my old starting_after cursor gets HTTP 410. Authentication is configured: the job belongs to the credential labelled CLIENT_A, while CLIENT_B is a different credential and cannot retrieve it. Please distinguish reader retention, owner access, job terminal state, native DONE and FIFO release. I do not want missed tool events silently skipped or any tool action executed twice. A strict JSON/tool response may have buffered partial output before cancellation; don't treat that as executable or token-level constrained decoding.

Give a safe recovery and stopping plan without contacting the service, broadcasting native STOP, killing the shared process, downloading anything, or claiming you reproduced the backend behavior. Also show an offline background text request using the bundled helper and explain the explicit store requirement.
